rules.description: Fail unexplained literal values in the primary Rust function encoding meaningful tunable domain policy: numerical convergence thresholds, tolerances, floors, optimizer bounds/steps, iteration budgets, byte/resource admission allowances, ordering dependencies on numeric codes, or sentinel ranks. A named constant or enum should communicate the policy. Naming the calculated result budget, tolerance or rank does not explain embedded coefficients. Unexplained per-record byte allowances and fixed byte overhead in a resource estimate fail; do not guess a concrete storage-layout derivation that the supplied context does not show. These are readability violations even when the computation is correct; do not require a runtime bug or an explicit documentation contract. Mathematical identities, locally explained wire/storage layouts or status encoding, zero/one flags and standard unit conversions pass. Context may explain a primary-unit literal, but a literal appearing only in a supplied callee is not a finding against its caller.
exceptions: Mathematical formula coefficients, coordinate geometry, interpolation, normalization, bit masks and algorithmic identities pass when the formula is recognizable; tunable convergence/tolerance policy is not a mathematical identity.

Wire/transport/storage field widths, offsets, buffer counts and status codes defined or decoded adjacently with a clear mapping or declared layout pass. Numeric diagnostic/status assignments or explicit equality/match decoding in clearly named branches are legitimate encoding, not tunable policy; opaque numeric ordering comparisons deciding domain policy do not pass.
Zero/one initialization, Boolean flags, empty values, simple indices/loop bounds and standard unit conversions pass.
Named constants, parameters, or adjacent comments explaining both the policy and choice of value pass.

rules.description: Functions should operate mostly at one conceptual level. Fail Rust high-level orchestration interleaved with substantial low-level encoding/decoding, parsing or storage-layout work that has its own coherent useful name. Manual character classification, nibble/byte assembly, framing or checksumming among domain operations is an independent codec responsibility, not incidental glue. Small calculations, field access, validation and ordinary adapters pass. A runtime defect or reusable public abstraction is not required; one allocation-free named helper can clarify responsibility.
exceptions: Small calculations, field access, validation and incidental serialization glue pass.
A focused implementation of an algorithm or codec, rather than orchestration, passes.
Named helpers that already isolate coherent low-level work pass.

rules.description: The attached Rustdoc must accurately describe the Rust code. Fail concrete contradictions in promised behavior/results or # Errors, # Panics and # Safety: claiming invalid input returns Err while parsing unwraps, claiming no errors while propagating a fallible parse, claiming no panics while indexing unchecked, claiming any pointer including null/dangling/unaligned is allowed while dereferencing it, or claiming complete persistence while writes/errors are ignored. These are inaccurate claims, not merely missing documentation. No doc comment, absent headings and unclaimed detail pass; native missing_errors_doc, missing_panics_doc and missing_safety_doc own completeness. Compare documented claims with visible body and supplied callees/types, and abstain only when the claimed behavior cannot be resolved.
exceptions: No Rustdoc, missing sections and merely incomplete detail pass.
Proved invariant unwraps do not contradict recovery claims for invalid input.
Documented permitted panics/preconditions and accurate safety requirements pass.
